h1: Investor Renovation Contractor in El Paso
intro: El Paso is a brick-and-stucco city in the high desert, and its houses fail in ways that investors from the rest of Texas do not always expect. Flat and low-slope roofs with parapets leak at the scuppers and around rooftop evaporative coolers. Older adobe and brick walls crack when the soil under them gets wet, not when it dries. Buyers and tenants increasingly want refrigerated air instead of swamp coolers, which turns an HVAC replacement into a ductwork project. And a hard freeze, like the one in 2011, can split pipes across the whole city. Genstone Construction coordinates vetted, licensed contractors in El Paso for investors, lenders and servicers, managed by our estimators and field managers from headquarters in Romeoville, Illinois. A free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices those repairs and checks your ARV before you commit, and every project runs on a detailed scope, a draw schedule tied to finished work and one field manager throughout.
housingStock:
El Paso's older neighborhoods wrap around the Franklin Mountains, and each one reflects a different chapter of the city's growth.

The oldest stock sits near downtown and the border. Segundo Barrio and Chihuahuita hold brick tenements and adobe and brick row houses from the late 1800s and early 1900s, many still occupied and many in need of structural and systems work. Sunset Heights, on the hill northwest of downtown, has Victorian, Queen Anne and early twentieth-century brick homes, and it is a designated historic district. Kern Place, near UTEP, has a mix of 1910s through 1930s houses in Pueblo Revival, Craftsman and Tudor styles. Manhattan Heights and Austin Terrace, east of downtown, were built mostly in the 1920s with brick bungalows, Tudor cottages and Spanish eclectic houses.

Brick is the dominant material in the older city, often with plaster interiors and flat or low-slope roofs behind parapets. Foundations are typically shallow concrete or stone footings rather than the pier-and-beam common elsewhere in Texas.

After World War II, the city spread northeast toward Fort Bliss and east into areas like Cielo Vista, Eastwood and the neighborhoods around them, with brick and stucco ranches on slabs, many with rooftop evaporative coolers and single-pane steel or aluminum windows. The Lower Valley and Mission Valley mix older adobe and brick homes with postwar ranches on former farmland near the river. From the 1980s onward, large tract subdivisions filled the far east, northeast and west sides, built of frame and stucco with refrigerated air. The constant factor across eras is the desert: intense sun on roofs and stucco, dry soils that react when water gets into them, and occasional extreme cold that catches unprepared plumbing.

commonIssues.title: Flat roofs, parapets and cooler curbs
commonIssues.body: Many El Paso homes have flat or low-slope roofs behind parapet walls, drained through scuppers and canales. Over years of sun, the roofing membrane cracks, parapet caps loosen and scuppers clog, and leaks appear during monsoon storms. Rooftop evaporative coolers add another penetration that often leaks around the curb. We inspect the membrane, parapets, flashing and drainage closely and price a full roof system replacement when patching would just postpone the next leak.

commonIssues.title: Soil settlement when wet
commonIssues.body: Some El Paso soils, particularly in areas built on arroyo fill or loose sandy deposits, can settle when they become saturated. A leaking supply line, a broken sewer or poor roof drainage near a wall can cause one corner of a brick house to drop, producing stair-step cracks and sticking doors. On older homes we look for those cracks, check the plumbing for leaks and recommend a foundation evaluation before you finalize your offer.

commonIssues.title: Swamp coolers versus refrigerated air
commonIssues.body: Evaporative coolers are still common on older El Paso homes, but many buyers and tenants now expect refrigerated air, especially during humid monsoon weeks when coolers lose efficiency. Converting requires new equipment, properly sized ductwork, electrical capacity and sometimes structural support. Ducts designed for a cooler are usually too large and leaky for refrigerated air. We price conversion properly rather than dropping a unit on old ducts that will not perform.

commonIssues.title: Cracked stucco and brick
commonIssues.body: Desert sun, temperature swings and soil movement crack stucco and brick, and unsealed cracks let monsoon rain into the walls. On older brick homes, deteriorated mortar joints need repointing with an appropriate mortar, and in historic districts the mortar and brick should match the original. We include stucco repair, brick repointing and sealing in scopes where needed, because water getting into the wall is often the root of interior damage.

commonIssues.title: Freeze-damaged plumbing
commonIssues.body: El Paso rarely freezes hard, but when it does, many homes are unprepared. The February 2011 freeze burst pipes throughout the city, especially lines in exterior walls, attics and on rooftops feeding evaporative coolers. Vacant homes were hit hard. We check plumbing routing, replace damaged or outdated lines, insulate exposed piping and make sure cooler supply lines can be drained for winter.

investorMarket:
El Paso's investor activity follows its biggest economic anchors: Fort Bliss, UTEP, the medical center and cross-border trade.

Northeast El Paso, closest to Fort Bliss, has brick ranches from the 1950s through the 1970s that rent steadily to military households and civilian workers. These houses fit BRRRR and long-term rental strategies well, and scopes center on roofs, cooling, windows and interiors. The far east and northeast tract neighborhoods trade more like suburban product, where investors focus on rental turns.

Central neighborhoods such as Manhattan Heights, Five Points, Kern Place and Sunset Heights attract flippers and investors who appreciate older brick homes with character, as well as small multifamily buyers. Sunset Heights and Kern Place are close to UTEP, which supports student and young professional rentals. Historic districts in Sunset Heights and Manhattan Heights add review for exterior work.

The Lower Valley and Mission Valley offer older homes at lower price points, often with adobe or brick construction and deferred maintenance. These suit buy-and-hold and BRRRR investors willing to take on systems, roof and structural work. Segundo Barrio and Chihuahuita contain older brick tenements and row houses that require experience with historic masonry and occupied buildings.

The west side and Upper Valley have higher-priced homes where flips focus on design and finish quality. Across all areas, El Paso's prices are generally lower than other large Texas metros, so careful budgeting and accurate ARVs matter.
permits:
Residential permits inside the city are issued by the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department. Structural work, foundation repair, additions, re-roofing, new or altered plumbing and electrical, HVAC installations including swamp cooler to refrigerated air conversions, and window changes that alter openings generally require permits and inspections. Trade permits must be pulled by contractors licensed through the Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners or the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation.

El Paso has local historic districts, including Sunset Heights, Manhattan Heights and Magoffin, along with individually designated landmarks. Exterior changes in these areas, such as window replacement, roofing materials visible from the street, porch alterations, masonry work and additions, need review through the city's historic preservation program and the Historic Landmark Commission. Masonry repair in historic districts is expected to match original materials.

Stormwater and drainage matter in El Paso because monsoon storms send heavy runoff through arroyos and streets. Additions and site work may need to address drainage. Addresses in Socorro, Horizon City, Anthony or unincorporated El Paso County fall under their own permitting offices. We confirm jurisdiction and district status before scoping.
climate:
El Paso's high desert climate is dominated by sun, heat and dryness, punctuated by short bursts of extreme weather. Summers are hot, and intense ultraviolet light degrades roofing membranes, sealants, paint and stucco faster than in more humid cities. Roofing and exterior work are often scheduled for mornings in summer.

The monsoon season brings sudden, intense thunderstorms, usually in mid to late summer, that can drop heavy rain in a short time. The 2006 floods damaged homes across the city. Roofs with clogged scuppers, cracked parapets and failing cooler curbs leak, and poor drainage near foundations can trigger soil settlement. Spring brings strong winds and dust. Winters are mild but freezes do occur, and the 2011 freeze burst pipes citywide. We plan roofing before monsoon season and include freeze protection in scopes.

faqs.q: Do you work in Socorro, Horizon City and other El Paso County areas?
faqs.a: Yes. We coordinate licensed contractors across the El Paso area, including Socorro, Horizon City, Canutillo, Anthony, Clint, Vinton and unincorporated El Paso County. Each jurisdiction has its own permitting and inspection process. We confirm which office covers each address before scoping, so the permit plan reflects the right authority and the schedule is realistic from the start. We can also look at properties just across the line in Santa Teresa and Sunland Park, New Mexico, though those follow New Mexico rules.

faqs.q: Should I convert a swamp cooler house to refrigerated air?
faqs.a: In many cases, yes, especially for flips and rentals in neighborhoods where buyers and tenants expect refrigerated air. Conversion usually means new equipment, new or modified ductwork sized for refrigerated air, electrical upgrades and roof work to remove or seal the old cooler opening. We price the full conversion so you can compare cost against the effect on sale price or rent.

faqs.q: How do you handle flat roof leaks on older El Paso homes?
faqs.a: We inspect the roofing membrane, parapet caps, flashing, scuppers and any rooftop equipment penetrations. Small, isolated problems can be repaired, but aged membranes with widespread cracking usually need replacement. We also clear and correct drainage so water leaves the roof quickly during monsoon storms, since standing water and clogged scuppers cause many interior leaks. Where a rooftop cooler is being removed, the curb opening is framed in and roofed over as part of the same job.

faqs.q: Do I pay anything upfront?
faqs.a: No. Genstone does not take upfront payment on El Paso projects. Draws are released against completed stages of work that you can verify through photos and milestone documentation, and the final payment comes after completion and your approval. Dumpster and debris costs are part of every estimate. A one-year workmanship warranty backs what we build in El Paso, excluding tenant damage and normal wear.

fix-flip.title: Fix and Flip Contractor in El Paso, TX | Genstone
fix-flip.metaDescription: El Paso fix and flip renovations for Kern Place, Manhattan Heights and west-side buyers: refrigerated air, new flat roofs, stucco and brick repair, fast draws.
fix-flip.h1: Fix and Flip Renovations in El Paso
fix-flip.intro: El Paso buyers judge a flip by three things their counterparts in Houston or Dallas rarely think about: whether the house has refrigerated air instead of a swamp cooler, whether the flat roof will survive the next monsoon, and whether the stucco and brick are sound. A flip in Manhattan Heights, Kern Place or the west side that gets those right and pairs them with a modern kitchen and baths tends to sell well. One that skips them gets renegotiated after inspection. Genstone builds El Paso flip scopes around those priorities. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the work, checks historic district status and refines your ARV before you commit capital, and our field manager coordinates licensed local contractors through permits, inspections and finish work so the house reaches the market ready for El Paso buyers.

sections.h2: What El Paso buyers expect from a renovated house
sections.body:
Most El Paso buyers now expect refrigerated air, and a flip that still relies on a swamp cooler will lose buyers or face a price reduction. Converting usually means new equipment, ductwork sized for refrigerated air, electrical upgrades and removing or sealing the old cooler opening. We plan that conversion as part of the core scope rather than an afterthought.

The roof is the second priority. Flat and low-slope roofs behind parapets need a sound membrane, intact parapet caps and clear scuppers. A buyer's inspector will climb up and check them, and monsoon season will test them. Exterior stucco and brick should be free of open cracks and properly sealed. Inside, buyers want updated kitchens and baths, durable tile or vinyl plank flooring, good lighting and energy-efficient windows that cut the afternoon heat. In older central neighborhoods, they also appreciate original details like arched doorways, hardwood floors and decorative tile. We price multiple finish levels so you can match what comparable sales in your neighborhood support.

sections.h2: Kern Place, Manhattan Heights and the west side
sections.body:
El Paso's flip opportunities differ by neighborhood. Manhattan Heights and Austin Terrace offer 1920s brick bungalows and Tudor and Spanish eclectic houses with character that buyers value. Scopes there typically include rewiring, plumbing replacement, refrigerated air, roof work, masonry repointing and careful kitchen and bath design that respects the house. Manhattan Heights is a historic district, so exterior changes need review.

Kern Place, close to UTEP, has a mix of older homes that appeal to faculty, professionals and buyers who want walkability to campus and Cincinnati Street. Houses there vary widely in condition and style, so scopes are highly individual. The west side and Upper Valley offer newer and higher-priced homes where flips focus on modern layouts, high-quality finishes and outdoor living space. In the northeast and east, brick ranches compete on price, condition and systems. Our Pre-Offer Rehab Review identifies which approach fits the specific house and street, and whether the purchase price leaves room for it once roof, cooling and masonry are priced honestly.

sections.h2: Scheduling around permits and the monsoon
sections.body:
El Paso flips lose money when the schedule slips, and two things most often cause delays: approvals and weather. In historic districts like Sunset Heights and Manhattan Heights, exterior work may need review before it can start. We identify those items early, submit promptly and sequence interior work so crews keep moving.

Roofing should be completed before monsoon season whenever possible. A house with a torn-off roof during a July storm is a costly problem. Summer heat also affects roofing and stucco work, which crews handle early in the day. Permits for structural, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and roofing work go through the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department, and our field manager schedules inspections in sequence to avoid idle time. Draws are tied to completed work and documented with milestone photos, so you can follow progress remotely and keep lenders or partners informed. Refrigerated air equipment and replacement windows are ordered as soon as the scope is final, which keeps those items from holding up the finish trades.

faqs.q: Is refrigerated air required to sell an El Paso flip?
faqs.a: Not legally, but in many neighborhoods buyers expect it, and a swamp cooler can narrow your buyer pool or lead to price reductions. In some older central neighborhoods and lower price ranges, a well-maintained cooler may still be acceptable. We compare recent sales in your area and price the conversion so you can decide based on the comps rather than guesswork.

faqs.q: How do I know if an El Paso flat roof needs replacing?
faqs.a: Signs include widespread cracking or blistering in the membrane, ponding water, deteriorated parapet caps, clogged or damaged scuppers and interior water stains. A roof that has been patched repeatedly is often near the end of its life. We inspect the roof during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review and price repair or replacement so the buyer's inspector does not find surprises. A new roof with a transferable warranty is also an easy point to make in the listing.

faqs.q: Can I change windows on a Manhattan Heights flip?
faqs.a: In the Manhattan Heights historic district, replacing windows visible from the street generally requires review, and the city prefers replacements that match the original design or repair of original windows. We check district guidelines and price both restoration and approved replacement so you can compare cost, schedule and the effect on sale price. Rear windows that are not visible from the street are often treated with more flexibility, which can lower the overall window budget.

brrrr.title: BRRRR Rehab Contractor in El Paso, TX | Genstone
brrrr.metaDescription: El Paso BRRRR rehabs near Fort Bliss and in the Lower Valley: brick ranch scopes, roof and cooling upgrades and rental-grade finishes that support the refi.
brrrr.intro: El Paso's lower price points and steady rental demand from Fort Bliss, UTEP, the medical center and cross-border commerce make it a natural BRRRR market. The likeliest candidates tend to be brick ranches in Northeast El Paso and the east side, and older brick and adobe homes in the Lower Valley and central neighborhoods that need a full systems update. The renovation must support a refinance appraisal and then hold up to tenants in a harsh, sunny climate. Genstone scopes El Paso BRRRR projects with both in mind. Before you buy, our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review puts numbers on both the repairs and the ARV, and if you want the refinance lined up at the same time, Genstone Financial writes DSCR rental loans. One field manager coordinates licensed local contractors, permits and inspections, with documented progress at every draw.

sections.h2: Renovating to the El Paso appraisal
sections.body:
El Paso appraisers compare your property to nearby sales and adjust for condition, cooling type and functional issues. Refrigerated air often carries weight in the comparison, especially in neighborhoods where most comparable sales have it. A sound roof, updated electrical and plumbing, modern windows and clean stucco or brick all help the appraisal more than high-end finishes do.

For BRRRR, we focus spending on the items that drive value and reduce tenant calls: the roof system, cooling, electrical panel, plumbing, windows and kitchens and baths finished to the level comparable rentals support. In Northeast El Paso and the east side, that usually means durable tile or vinyl plank, mid-range counters and standard fixtures. Spending beyond what the comps support rarely moves the appraisal. We also check for unpermitted additions and enclosed carports or garages, which are common, and price legalization or removal so your ARV reflects what the appraiser will count.

El Paso's sun and temperature swings are hard on materials. Roofing membranes, sealants, exterior paint and caulk degrade faster here than in more humid climates, and stucco cracks over time. A rental scope should use materials that tolerate intense ultraviolet exposure: reflective roof coatings or membranes, quality exterior sealants and paint systems designed for high-sun environments.

Inside, we choose tile or waterproof vinyl plank, scrubbable paint, solid cabinets and standard fixtures that can be replaced easily. For cooling, refrigerated air reduces tenant complaints during monsoon humidity and can support higher rent, while well-maintained evaporative coolers can still work in some lower-priced rentals with lower operating costs. We discuss the trade-offs with you. Plumbing is routed and insulated to reduce freeze risk, and cooler supply lines are set up so they can be drained for winter. These choices lower turnover costs and help protect the value you need for the next refinance.

sections.h2: El Paso neighborhoods that fit BRRRR
sections.body:
Northeast El Paso near Fort Bliss is one of the most common BRRRR areas. Brick ranches there rent steadily to military households and civilian workers, and scopes typically center on roof, cooling, windows, electrical and interiors. The east side, including Cielo Vista, Eastwood and nearby areas, offers similar housing with steady demand.

The Lower Valley and Mission Valley offer older brick and adobe homes at lower prices, with scopes that may include foundation evaluation, roof replacement, rewiring, plumbing and cooling upgrades. Central neighborhoods like Five Points and Manhattan Heights can also work, especially near UTEP and the medical center, though historic district rules may add cost to exterior work. During the Pre-Offer Rehab Review, we evaluate the roof, foundation, systems and any additions, and give you a realistic scope and ARV so you can see whether the refinance works before you buy. Because El Paso purchase prices are lower than in other large Texas cities, a misjudged roof or cooling conversion takes a bigger bite out of the margin, which is why we price those items carefully up front.

faqs.q: Can Genstone Financial refinance my El Paso rental?
faqs.a: Genstone Financial, the lending company within the Genstone Companies, offers DSCR rental loans in addition to fix-and-flip loans, lines of credit and new construction loans. DSCR loans qualify on the property's rental income, which works for many BRRRR investors. You are free to choose any lender, and we provide the same scope, draw records and completion documentation either way, including roof and cooling details the appraiser will ask about.

faqs.q: Do I need refrigerated air in an El Paso rental?
faqs.a: It depends on the neighborhood and rent level. In many areas, refrigerated air is expected and supports higher rent and fewer complaints. In some lower-priced rentals, a well-maintained evaporative cooler can still lease well and costs tenants less to run. We review comparable rentals and price both options so you can choose what fits your numbers. Either way, the system should be serviced and documented before the first tenant moves in.

faqs.q: How do you handle military tenants near Fort Bliss?
faqs.a: Military households often relocate on predictable cycles and expect clean, safe, well-maintained homes. We focus on reliable cooling and heating, sound roofs, secure doors and windows, durable finishes and good curb appeal so properties lease quickly and handle frequent turnover. Proximity to the base matters more than high-end finishes, so we keep the budget on the systems and durability items that prevent calls between moves.

rental-renovation.title: Rental Property Renovation in El Paso, TX | Genstone
rental-renovation.metaDescription: El Paso single-family rental renovations: brick ranches near Fort Bliss, east-side tract homes and Lower Valley houses held to one desert-ready standard.
rental-renovation.h1: Rental Property Renovations in El Paso
rental-renovation.intro: Single-family rentals in El Paso fall into a few clear groups: brick ranches in Northeast El Paso and the east side that house military and civilian families, newer frame-and-stucco tract homes in the far east, northeast and west sides, and older brick and adobe homes in the Lower Valley and central neighborhoods. Each group fails differently under the desert sun, the monsoon and the occasional hard freeze. Genstone works with landlords, funds and institutional owners to renovate and turn rental homes across El Paso and nearby communities. We coordinate licensed local contractors, apply one written portfolio standard adjusted for each house type, and assign a single field manager to each property. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps acquisitions teams price houses before purchase, and our scopes and draw records give asset managers a clear picture of spending.

sections.h2: A rental standard written for the desert
sections.body:
Our El Paso portfolio standard starts from the same baseline every rental needs: durable tile or waterproof vinyl plank, a single paint family, standard cabinet sizes and fixtures, working smoke and carbon monoxide alarms and secure locks. Where it departs from a generic spec is in the parts of the house the climate attacks.

Roofs are first. Flat and low-slope roofs get inspected for membrane condition, parapet caps, flashing and scupper drainage, and we favor reflective membranes or coatings that hold up to intense sun. Cooling is second. Each property gets a documented decision on refrigerated air versus a well-maintained evaporative cooler, based on rent level and neighborhood, and cooler supply lines are set up to drain for winter. Exterior stucco and brick are sealed so monsoon rain stays out of the walls. Plumbing is checked for leaks near foundations, since water in the soil can cause settlement in some El Paso areas, and exposed lines are insulated against freezes. Interior choices favor materials that tolerate dust and heavy use. Applying that standard consistently keeps per-unit costs predictable and makes future turns faster.

sections.h2: Managing a portfolio across El Paso County
sections.body:
Many El Paso portfolios extend beyond city limits into Socorro, Horizon City, Canutillo, Anthony and unincorporated El Paso County, where much of the newer tract housing sits. Each jurisdiction has its own permitting and inspection process, and some newer subdivisions have homeowners associations with exterior rules. A portfolio program has to account for those differences while keeping quality and pricing consistent.

Genstone keeps one written scope standard and one documentation format across the whole footprint, while licensed, insured contractors in our network perform the work locally. Each property gets a field manager who handles permits, inspections, lien waivers and contractor compliance in the right jurisdiction. Photo milestones and draw requests arrive in your inbox, so nobody has to fly in to check on a turn. Our estimators also flag properties that need capital work beyond a turn, such as a roof near the end of its life, a swamp cooler to refrigerated air conversion, a foundation showing settlement, or stucco failure letting water into walls, so annual budgets reflect actual conditions.

sections.h2: Turns timed around heat, monsoon and freeze
sections.body:
El Paso's seasons give rental turns a natural rhythm. Spring turns are the natural window to service or replace cooling equipment and to convert coolers to refrigerated air, before summer heat drives up demand for HVAC contractors. Early summer turns, before the monsoon, are the right time to inspect and repair roofs, clear scuppers and seal stucco cracks. Fall turns are a good time to drain cooler lines, insulate exposed plumbing and check heating systems before the first cold snap.

We scope turns to catch these predictable issues rather than just repaint and clean. That includes checking roof drainage, testing alarms, rekeying, servicing cooling and heating systems, checking water heater age and pressure relief valves, resealing tubs and showers and looking for new wall cracks. Genstone Field Services also provides occupied maintenance, inspections and code compliance between tenancies, so one organization can handle both renovation and upkeep. Our one-year workmanship warranty applies to work we complete, with tenant damage and normal wear excluded.

faqs.q: Do you renovate rentals outside El Paso city limits?
faqs.a: Yes. We work in Socorro, Horizon City, Canutillo, Anthony, Clint and unincorporated El Paso County, where a lot of newer rental housing sits. Each area has its own permit office and inspection process, and some subdivisions have HOA rules. We confirm local requirements for each address and apply your portfolio standard so finishes, pricing and reporting stay consistent across the portfolio.

faqs.q: Should I replace swamp coolers across my El Paso portfolio?
faqs.a: Not necessarily all at once. Refrigerated air tends to support higher rents and fewer complaints, especially during monsoon humidity, but it costs more to install and run. Many owners convert as units turn over or as coolers fail, starting with properties where comparable rentals already have refrigerated air. We price each conversion so you can plan the rollout across the portfolio.

faqs.q: How do you protect El Paso rentals from freeze damage?
faqs.a: We check plumbing routing for lines in exterior walls, attics and rooftops, insulate exposed piping and make sure evaporative cooler supply lines can be drained for winter. After the 2011 freeze damaged plumbing across the city, these steps became routine in our scopes. We also show tenants where the main shutoff is, which limits damage if a line does split.

multifamily-renovation.title: Duplex & Fourplex Renovation in El Paso, TX | Genstone
multifamily-renovation.metaDescription: El Paso 2–4 unit renovations: Central and Five Points brick fourplexes, UTEP-area duplexes and Northeast units near Fort Bliss, phased around tenants.
multifamily-renovation.h1: Small Multifamily Renovations in El Paso
multifamily-renovation.intro: El Paso has a long history of small multifamily housing. Central El Paso, Five Points and Manhattan Heights contain brick duplexes and fourplexes from the 1920s through the 1950s, often with flat roofs, parapets and courtyard layouts. Near UTEP, in Kern Place and Sunset Heights, older houses and small buildings rent to students and staff. Northeast El Paso near Fort Bliss has brick duplexes and fourplexes from the 1960s and 1970s. And closer to the border, Segundo Barrio holds older brick tenements and row houses that require experience with historic masonry and occupied buildings. Genstone helps investors renovate 2–4 unit buildings across El Paso by coordinating licensed local contractors, phasing work around tenants and managing permits and historic reviews. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review prices the work before you buy.

sections.h2: Older brick buildings in Central El Paso and Five Points
sections.body:
The brick duplexes and fourplexes of Central El Paso, Five Points and Manhattan Heights are solidly built but usually tired. Their flat roofs and parapets have often been patched many times, scuppers clog, and leaks run into upper-unit ceilings. Electrical service is frequently undersized for modern use, with older wiring in some units. Plumbing may include galvanized supply and cast-iron drains shared among units. Many units still rely on evaporative coolers, sometimes one per unit on the roof, each adding a penetration.

Our scopes for these buildings typically start with the roof system, since water intrusion damages everything below it. Then we address electrical service upgrades and separate metering where practical, plumbing replacement, cooling upgrades that fit the building, masonry repointing and stucco repair. Kitchens and baths are updated with durable, standard finishes. Courtyard layouts make access easier but require attention to shared walkways, stairs and lighting. Buildings in Manhattan Heights or other historic districts need review for exterior changes, which we plan for from the start.

sections.h2: Northeast units near Fort Bliss and UTEP-area rentals
sections.body:
Brick duplexes and fourplexes in Northeast El Paso were built largely in the 1960s and 1970s to house military and civilian workers, and they continue to rent steadily. These buildings sit on slabs and typically need roof work, cooling upgrades, window replacement, electrical panel updates and interior refreshes. Units turn over frequently with military moves, so durable finishes and simple, standard fixtures pay off.

Near UTEP, in Kern Place and Sunset Heights, older houses divided into units and small buildings rent to students and staff. These properties often have shared utilities, limited fire separation between units and older electrical and plumbing. Sunset Heights is a historic district, so exterior work needs review. We scope electrical upgrades, plumbing replacement, fire separation and smoke detection, cooling and durable interiors. Because these buildings often have tenants, we phase work unit by unit, complete vacant units first and schedule shared-system work with notice. Genstone Field Services can handle occupied maintenance in units not yet renovated.

El Paso zoning determines how many units are allowed on a lot, and many older buildings in central neighborhoods predate current zoning and exist as nonconforming uses. That status generally allows continued use but can limit expansion and affect rebuilding after major damage. Confirming zoning and the legal number of units before you buy matters, especially when financing depends on unit count.

Renovation permits go through the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department. Exterior work in historic districts, including Sunset Heights and Manhattan Heights, requires review through the city's historic preservation program. Multi-unit buildings must meet fire and life-safety requirements for separation, egress and smoke detection. In occupied buildings, our field manager coordinates access, schedules shared shutoffs with written notice, keeps common areas and courtyards safe and documents progress. Roof replacement on occupied buildings is planned before monsoon season and staged so units are never left exposed. We map these requirements during the Pre-Offer Rehab Review so the scope and budget reflect compliance from day one.

faqs.q: Can you separate utilities in an El Paso fourplex?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Separating electrical service usually means a new meter bank and individual panels coordinated with El Paso Electric and the city's electrical inspection. Water separation is more difficult and depends on how the building is plumbed. Gas may already be separate in some buildings. We evaluate each utility and include feasible options in the scope so you can weigh the cost against tenant-paid utilities.

faqs.q: Do historic rules apply to a Sunset Heights duplex?
faqs.a: If the building is in the Sunset Heights historic district, exterior changes such as windows, roofing visible from the street, porches, masonry and additions require review. Interior work is generally not reviewed. We check status and plan exterior work to meet the guidelines, which often means repairing original features and matching masonry rather than replacing them with modern materials. Interior unit upgrades can usually proceed while any exterior application is reviewed.

faqs.q: How do you replace a flat roof on an occupied building?
faqs.a: We schedule roof replacement before monsoon season, stage the work so only sections are open at a time and keep temporary protection ready for sudden storms. Tenants get notice before work begins. Rooftop coolers are removed, replaced or relocated as part of the job, and penetrations are sealed properly so the new roof does not leak at the same old spots.

fha-203k.title: FHA 203(k) Contractor in El Paso, TX | Genstone
fha-203k.metaDescription: FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor in El Paso: flat roofs, refrigerated air conversions, masonry and foundation repair bid for Limited or Standard 203(k) loans.
fha-203k.intro: El Paso's lower home prices make the FHA 203(k) loan especially useful. A buyer can purchase an older brick bungalow in Manhattan Heights, a ranch in Northeast El Paso or an adobe home in the Lower Valley and finance the repairs it needs in the same mortgage, from a new flat roof and refrigerated air to masonry repair and updated wiring. Genstone Construction is an FHA 203(k) Certified Contractor, and we work with buyers, agents, lenders and HUD consultants across El Paso to prepare the line-item bids and draw schedules the program requires. We coordinate licensed local contractors to complete the work after closing and keep everyone informed through each draw. Our free Pre-Offer Rehab Review helps buyers understand likely repair costs before writing an offer, which keeps the deal realistic from the start.

sections.h2: Limited and Standard 203(k) for El Paso homes
sections.body:
The Limited 203(k) covers non-structural repairs up to $75,000 without a HUD consultant. In El Paso, it fits homes that need common updates: a flat roof replacement, conversion from a swamp cooler to refrigerated air, new windows, an electrical panel upgrade, plumbing replacement, flooring, paint and kitchen or bath work. Many brick ranches in Northeast El Paso and the east side fit this profile when the foundation is sound.

The Standard 203(k) is needed when the scope includes structural work. In El Paso, that may mean repairing foundation settlement from saturated soils, rebuilding deteriorated adobe or brick walls, replacing a failing roof structure or removing a load-bearing wall. The Standard program has a $5,000 minimum repair amount and requires a HUD consultant who inspects the home, prepares the write-up and approves draws. We coordinate with the consultant so our bid matches the write-up and the schedule puts structural work ahead of finishes.

sections.h2: Good El Paso candidates for the program
sections.body:
The strongest El Paso 203(k) candidates are homes in neighborhoods buyers want, priced down by problems that are visible and fixable. A 1920s brick bungalow in Manhattan Heights that needs a roof, rewiring, plumbing, refrigerated air and a kitchen is a typical project, though historic district review applies to exterior work. A 1960s ranch near Fort Bliss with an old swamp cooler, single-pane windows and a dated kitchen is a classic Limited project, and VA-eligible buyers sometimes compare it with a VA renovation option. A Lower Valley adobe home may need masonry, roof and systems work, sometimes structural.

Local cautions include unpermitted additions and enclosed carports, which may need to be legalized or removed for the loan to close, and lead-safe practices on homes built before 1978. In historic districts, exterior repairs like window replacement or masonry work may need approval. Spotting these during the first walkthrough lets the buyer, agent and loan officer build them into the offer and the bid instead of discovering them at appraisal.

sections.h2: Bids, draws and timing in El Paso
sections.body:
A 203(k) depends on clear documentation. The lender needs a contractor bid broken out by line item with labor and materials, and on a Standard loan the bid must match the consultant's write-up. After closing, repair funds are held and released in draws as work is completed and inspected, and projects above the $15,000 threshold involve extra inspection and paperwork at each stage.

Genstone's estimators prepare bids in the format El Paso lenders and consultants expect, and our field manager coordinates draw inspections as phases finish. We take no upfront payment and tie draws to completed work, which matches how the program releases funds. Permits go through the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department, and historic reviews are requested early when needed. Timing matters in El Paso: we schedule roof replacement before monsoon season when possible and order refrigerated air equipment early so buyers are not moving in during summer without cooling.

faqs.q: Can a 203(k) pay for converting a swamp cooler to refrigerated air?
faqs.a: Yes. Installing refrigerated air, including new equipment, ductwork, electrical upgrades and sealing the old cooler opening, is an eligible repair under both the Limited and Standard programs. We price the full conversion in the bid so the lender and buyer see the complete cost. Many El Paso buyers consider this one of the most valuable items in the loan, because it changes how the house feels from the first summer onward.

faqs.q: Does a 203(k) cover flat roof replacement?
faqs.a: Yes. Roof replacement is eligible under both programs. On El Paso flat roofs, we include the membrane, parapet cap repairs, flashing, scupper drainage and sealing of any old equipment penetrations. Scheduling the roof first, ideally before monsoon season, protects the interior work that follows and keeps draws moving in order. If the roof deck or framing under the membrane is rotted from past leaks, that repair can push the loan into Standard territory, so we look closely before finalizing the bid.

faqs.q: Do you work with El Paso agents and lenders?
faqs.a: Yes. El Paso agents tend to call us when a buyer falls for a house with a tired flat roof or an old cooler and needs to know whether the numbers work. We walk the property, give a realistic repair figure, then prepare the line-item bid for the lender. On Standard loans we work directly with the HUD consultant, and all parties receive the same draw updates through move-in.

reo-renovation.title: REO & Bank-Owned Renovation in El Paso, TX | Genstone
reo-renovation.metaDescription: El Paso REO renovation for servicers, banks and GSEs: monsoon roof leaks, freeze-split pipes, stolen coolers, stucco damage and code compliance, documented.
reo-renovation.h1: REO and Bank-Owned Property Renovation in El Paso
reo-renovation.intro: Vacant bank-owned homes in El Paso deteriorate in ways shaped by the desert. Flat roofs that no one maintains leak during monsoon storms, soaking ceilings and walls. Rooftop coolers and refrigerated air units are stolen, leaving open curbs that let in rain. Freezes split pipes in homes that were never winterized, and water that soaks into the ground near a foundation can cause settlement. Stucco cracks, yards fill with weeds and debris, and code complaints follow. Genstone works with mortgage servicers, banks, REITs, investment funds and Government-Sponsored Enterprises, which use us as a preferred contractor, to stabilize and renovate REO properties across El Paso. Genstone Field Services handles property preservation, inspections and code compliance, and our construction team manages repairs through licensed local contractors, with every condition and step documented.

sections.h2: What vacant El Paso homes typically need
sections.body:
Roof leaks are the most common serious issue in El Paso REO properties. Flat and low-slope roofs need regular maintenance, and when a house sits vacant, scuppers clog, membranes crack and parapet caps loosen. The first monsoon storm sends water through ceilings and down walls, damaging drywall, insulation and flooring and sometimes leading to mold. Stolen rooftop coolers or condensers leave open curbs that make the problem worse.

Freeze damage is another recurring finding. When El Paso sees a hard freeze, plumbing in exterior walls, attics and on rooftops can split, and in a vacant home the leak can run for a long time before anyone notices. Water soaking into the soil near the foundation can cause settlement and new cracks in brick or stucco. Vandalism and theft are common, including stolen cooling equipment, copper wiring and appliances. The first site visit produces a photo report and a rough scope, giving the servicer enough to choose between repairing and selling as-is without a long back-and-forth.

sections.h2: Stabilizing and preparing El Paso REO homes
sections.body:
El Paso REO work usually starts with stabilization: securing doors and windows, covering open roof curbs, clearing scuppers, winterizing plumbing, removing debris and addressing immediate hazards. Genstone Field Services carries out most of this preservation work. Repairs then focus on items that affect value or financing, such as roof replacement, plumbing repair, cooling equipment, electrical work, stucco and masonry repair and any foundation issues. Listing preparation follows with paint, flooring, cleaning and yard cleanup.

Our estimators can price several options for each property. A light scope supports an as-is sale to investors, while a fuller scope that meets FHA and VA minimum property requirements opens the home to owner-occupant buyers, including the many military households near Fort Bliss. Comparing those options helps asset managers estimate net recovery. Dumpster and debris removal is included in every estimate, and draws are tied to completed, documented work so asset managers can follow progress remotely.

sections.h2: Code compliance, permits and records in El Paso
sections.body:
City code enforcement in El Paso responds to vacant-property problems such as overgrown weeds, accumulated trash, open or unsecured structures and unsafe conditions, and unresolved violations can lead to citations and liens. Genstone Field Services monitors properties on a schedule, keeps yards clear and responds to notices quickly so violations do not build up while the asset is marketed.

When repair work begins, permits go through the City of El Paso Planning and Inspections Department or the appropriate office for Socorro, Horizon City or unincorporated El Paso County. Roofing, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work each need permits and inspections, and we keep the sign-offs with the project file. Properties in historic districts like Sunset Heights or Manhattan Heights need review for exterior changes, which we plan for early. Lien waivers and contractor compliance documentation are collected on every job and organized for audit, so servicers and buyers have a complete record of what was repaired and permitted.

faqs.q: Do you winterize vacant El Paso homes?
faqs.a: Yes. Genstone Field Services winterizes plumbing by draining supply lines, protecting traps and shutting off water service, and we pay particular attention to rooftop cooler lines and pipes in exterior walls. After a freeze, we inspect previously winterized homes and document their condition so servicers know whether repairs are needed before the next showing. Because hard freezes are rare in El Paso, many vacant houses are left unprepared, and a quick post-freeze check prevents a small split from becoming a flooded slab.

faqs.q: Can you secure a roof after cooler equipment is stolen?
faqs.a: Yes. When a rooftop cooler or condenser is stolen, the open curb or penetration needs to be covered quickly to prevent rain from entering, especially during monsoon season. We provide temporary protection immediately, then price permanent repair, whether that means replacing the equipment or framing in and roofing over the opening as part of a cooling conversion. Photos of the theft and the temporary repair go to the servicer the same day for insurance and reporting.

faqs.q: Do you cover REO homes across El Paso County?
faqs.a: Yes. Our licensed contractor network covers El Paso and nearby communities including Socorro, Horizon City, Canutillo, Anthony and unincorporated El Paso County. Each property gets a field manager and consistent documentation, and we confirm the correct permitting and code office for each address before work starts. Reports follow a single format across the pool, so a servicer reviewing a Socorro house and a Northeast El Paso house sees the same layout, photo set and draw history for each.
